newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai subway contract to be signed on Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: Thai subway contract to be signed on Nov 5.

text.p: A 24 billion baht (US$944 million) contract awarded to a Thai-German-Japanese consortium to build Thailand's first subway system will be signed on November 5, a government official said on Friday.

The contract awarded by the Mass Rapid Transit Authority of Thailand (MRTA) would be signed by the MRTA with the BCKT consortium, comprising Thailand's Ch Karnchang Plc, Germany's Bilfinger and Berger, Japan's Tokyu Construction and Kumagai Gumi, he told Reuters.
Theerapong Attaijarusit, director of the state agency coordinating the project's development, said he would sign the contract on behalf of the MRTA.
Also present at the signing would be representatives of Japan's Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund which is funding a major portion of the project, he said.
Construction of the first 11 km (seven miles) of subway, in Bangkok, and nine stations is scheduled to begin in the first quarter of 1997, with the system operational by 2002.
Approval for the contract was awarded at a cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa.
Theerapong said he was optimistic any new government that came in after general elections on November 17 would not review the project.
